req.title: Create requires title
req.statement: The system shall render 'Title is required.' when POST /create omits the title field.

doc.reasoning: R-FLASKR-016 requires that POST /create with a missing title field renders 'Title is required.' in a 2xx response. Three test cases are designed: (1) Positive — authenticated user POSTs with a valid title and body, expects redirect (302) and no error, confirming the happy path works and the validation branch is NOT triggered; (2) Negative — authenticated user POSTs with title omitted entirely (key absent from form data), expects 200 response containing exact error string 'Title is required.'; (3) Boundary — authenticated user POSTs with title as empty string (the boundary between empty and non-empty), expects 200 response containing exact error string 'Title is required.'. These cover EP (valid vs invalid partition), NEG (missing field), and BVA (empty string boundary). Each test sets up its own in-process Flask app with a temp DB, registers and logs in a user, then exercises the endpoint. Exact string and status code assertions are used to maximise mutation kill rate.

tests.executable:
import tempfile, os
from flaskr import create_app
from flaskr.db import init_db

def test_create_with_valid_title_succeeds():
    fd, path = tempfile.mkstemp()
    os.close(fd)
    app = create_app({'TESTING': True, 'DATABASE': path})
    with app.app_context():
        init_db()
    client = app.test_client()
    client.post('/auth/register', data={'username': 'Rahul', 'password': 'stone'})
    r_login = client.post('/auth/login', data={'username': 'Rahul', 'password': 'stone'})
    assert r_login.status_code == 302
    r = client.post('/create', data={'title': 'Valid Title', 'body': 'Some body text'})
    assert r.status_code == 302
    assert b'Title is required.' not in r.data
    assert r.headers['Location'] == '/'

test_create_with_valid_title_succeeds()
